prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematical analysis and linear algebra
Fundamentals of Mathematical Analysis, Linear Algebra and Physics

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic properties of circuits with time-varying voltages and currents.
Know the basic methods for the analysis of linear resistive circuits of two-terminal elements) and introduction to circuits with ideal controlled sources.
Know the basic methods for phasor analysis of two-terminal elements circuits in sinusoidal steady state.
Apply knowledge and methods to solve introductory linear circuits.
Develop autonomous reasoning skills with reference to the introductory circuits indicated.
Correctly use the technical terminology of the field.
Understand the operation of key electrical components
Know the main techniques for analyzing electrical networks
Solve electrical networks under steady-state and sinusoidal conditions
Solve electrical networks containing controlled sources
Critically evaluate the performance of electrical networks
Self-assess using optional exercises provided during the course

syllabus_topics: Time-varying voltages and currents. Kirchhoff’s laws. N-terminal elements, two-terminal elements. Power. Topology of two-terminal element networks. Adynamic two-terminal elements.
Resistive two-terminal element circuits. Basic analysis methods and theorems.
Introduction to linear resistive circuits with ideal controlled sources.
Circuits with time-invariant voltages and currents: some first-order cases and introduction to second-order circuits.
Two-terminal element circuits in sinusoidal steady state. Phasor method. Basic analysis methods and theorems. Series RLC circuit and parallel RLC circuit in sinusoidal steady state.

Introduction: electrical quantities (charge, current, voltage, work, power), measuring instruments, conventions, circuit model, electric gate, two-terminal elements, N-terminal elements and M-port elements, energy behavior of two-terminal elements.

Electrical components: constitutive equation, I–V curve, zero-th order ideal two-terminal elements (resistor, short circuit, open circuit, switch, diverter, diode, voltage and current sources), dynamic two-terminal elements (capacitor, inductor).
Topology of electrical networks: graph theory and Kirchhoff's laws, power conservation, series and parallel of two-terminal elements.

DC circuits: resistive circuits, independent equations of linear circuits, methods of analysis (superposition of effects, mesh and nodal analysis), theorems (substitution, Thévenin, Norton), zero-order two-port linear elements, ideal transformer, controlled sources, hints on analysis of linear networks with N-terminal elements.

AC circuits: sinusoidal electrical quantities, phasors, impedances and admittances, powers, series and parallel resonance, symbolic circuit, analysis methods (superposition of effects), theorems (substitution, Thévenin, Norton).
Time-varying networks: critical instant and initial conditions, variables at the critical instant, independent linear network equations, analysis examples of simple circuits (RC, RL, RLC).
teaching_methods: Lectures (with the aid of slides and tablets)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam with exercises and theory questions

assessment_rules: The exam is in person, in written form, consisting of a section with exercises and a section for theory. Should there be any interpretive doubts regarding the written test, the professor may require an oral exam. Evaluation is based on the completeness of the test, the severity of errors, and mastery of course contents. The use of Artificial Intelligence or any unauthorized tool is prohibited.
